summary: UnityPlayer's low-integrity test: OpenProcessToken(current, TOKEN_QUERY) answers a handle, a multiple of 4; GetTokenInformation(TokenIntegrityLevel) answers 122 and 28 bytes with no buffer or one byte short, then a TOKEN_MANDATORY_LABEL (attributes 0x60, the SID at offset 16, revision 1, one sub-authority, authority 16) whose RID is not low; GetSidSubAuthority answers the field's address and last error 0; CloseHandle closes the token. LocalAlloc (LMEM_FIXED, LPTR) gives a 16-aligned process-heap block of the size asked, LPTR zeroed; LocalFree answers NULL.
applicability: windows-2022 (AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor); windows-2025 (AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor)

initial.process: started by the runner's cmd with standard output redirected

evidence.source_ref: run 38099150504: windows-2025, AMD EPYC 7763 64-Core Processor, probe sha256:6d84a44be6a006613661b693b1677cb0b096a17ceca4c5773975f329822f7456; run 38099152338: windows-2022, AMD EPYC 9V45 96-Core Processor, probe sha256:06e41e1e27336675a83949d6e2956998ed18b60a11742e5c006577a58091aac5

evidence.quote: Windows defines four integrity levels: low, medium, high, and system. Standard users receive medium, elevated users receive high.

open_questions: A runner's process is elevated and its RID is 0x3000 (high) on all four executions; w2m answers 0x2000 (medium), a standard user's level. The derive keeps whether the RID is low (0x1000), UnityPlayer's question at 0x180525de0.
